# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto itinerary built around temples, street food, and moderate walking, with later starts and lower-crowd timing in mind. Total trip spend is planned to stay close to your **$1,600** budget excluding international flights.

# Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

## Day 1 — April 10: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- **Late morning:** Arrive and check in, then ease into Kyoto with a slow walk around **Yasaka Shrine** and **Maruyama Park**.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kodai-ji** and nearby lanes in **Ninenzaka / Sannenzaka** for temple views and snack stops.
- **Dinner:** Street-food-style bites around **Gion** and **Shijo**; keep it light and flexible.
- **Rain backup:** **Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art** or **Kyoto National Museum**.

Daily cost estimate:
- Hotel: **$190**
- Food: **$70**
- Local transit: **$18**
- Admissions/snacks: **$32**
- Total: **$310**

## Day 2 — April 11: Arashiyama and West Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg

- **Late morning:** Head to **Arashiyama** after the early rush; start with **Tenryu-ji** and the **Bamboo Grove**.
- **Afternoon:** Cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**, then choose one lighter add-on: **Okochi Sanso Garden** or a riverside tea break.
- **Dinner:** Return toward central Kyoto for **ramen, yakitori, or tempura** near **Kawaramachi**.
- **Rain backup:** **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Saga-Arashiyama Station area cafes and shops**.

Daily cost estimate:
- Hotel: **$190**
- Food: **$75**
- Transit: **$22**
- Admissions/snacks: **$38**
- Total: **$325**

## Day 3 — April 12: Fushimi Inari and Southern Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- **Late morning:** Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** after the earliest crowd wave has passed; go only as far up the trail as feels comfortable.
- **Afternoon:** Continue to **Tofuku-ji** for a quieter temple atmosphere and garden time.
- **Dinner:** Explore **Fushimi** sake district or return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner and dessert stop.
- **Rain backup:** **Kyoto Museum of Crafts and Design** or **Kyoto Tower Sando** for indoor browsing and food.

Daily cost estimate:
- Hotel: **$190**
- Food: **$75**
- Transit: **$20**
- Admissions/snacks: **$30**
- Total: **$315**

## Day 4 — April 13: Northern Temples and Departure Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- **Late morning:** Choose one major northern temple area: **Kinkaku-ji** for the iconic gold pavilion or **Ryoan-ji** for a calmer, less rushed visit.
- **Afternoon:** If energy allows, add **Ninna-ji** or a slow café-and-shop stop in **Kitano**.
- **Dinner:** Final Kyoto meal near your hotel or station; aim for something easy before departure logistics.
- **Rain backup:** **Kyoto International Manga Museum** or **Nishiki Market covered lanes** for food and browsing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Rain backup:** **Kyoto International Manga Museum** or **Nishiki Market covered lanes** for food and browsing, Kyoto, Japan

Daily cost estimate:
- Hotel: **$190**
- Food: **$70**
- Transit: **$18**
- Admissions/snacks: **$28**
- Total: **$306**

## Budget Fit and Trip Balance

| Day | Focus | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---:|
| April 10 | Higashiyama, Gion, temple lanes | **$310** |
| April 11 | Arashiyama, bamboo grove, river views | **$325** |
| April 12 | Fushimi Inari, Tofuku-ji, sake district | **$315** |
| April 13 | Kinkaku-ji / Ryoan-ji, northern Kyoto | **$306** |

Trip total estimate: **$1,256**

Planned buffer for extra snacks, taxis, souvenirs, or a nicer dinner: **$344**

# Best Rhythm for Avoiding Crowds

- Start most days at **late morning** rather than dawn, but still visit the most famous spots before peak afternoon traffic.
- Prioritize **one major attraction per day** plus a nearby secondary stop to keep walking moderate.
- Use **taxi or short transit hops** when temple clusters are spread out.
- Build in **tea breaks** and market snacks instead of long restaurant meals.
